column1: # sensitive-terms-v1: GDPR Art. 9 special-category terms (K10, seal r1).
# One entry per line: CATEGORY <TAB> LANG <TAB> TERM
# CATEGORY  HEALTH | HEALTHCUE | RELIGION | SEXUAL_ORIENTATION | TRADE_UNION | ETHNIC_ORIGIN
#           HEALTHCUE lists the words that anchor a nearby ambiguous abbreviation.
# LANG      fr | en | af | hu | sl | zh | xx (any language; documentation only)
# TERM      Case, accents and full-width forms are folded before matching. A
#           trailing `*` marks a stem. The words of a multi-word term may be
#           separated by spaces, hyphens or apostrophes. A term with Han
#           characters matches as a substring, on a view where traditional
#           characters read as simplified ones. A leading `?` marks an ambiguous
#           abbreviation (MS, SEP, TOC, SM): it is masked only when a strong term
#           or a HEALTHCUE word shares its sentence. An exception line
#           `term|list` takes words away from a term: a Latin term lists the
#           words it must not match (`FIV|five,fives`), a Han term the suffix
#           that must not follow it (`中风|险`).
# Keep an entry unambiguous on its own. A bare nationality, a party name or a
# given name is never an entry.
# Brand names (lang xx) of common antidepressants, antipsychotics, anxiolytics,
# ADHD stimulants and HIV antiretrovirals. The list is not exhaustive. The names
# are not checked against the EMA register in this round: add a name only with
# NAMES-OFF r2 (2026-10-19): terms the name model used to hide by chance, and
# common conditions, care words and INN names of everyday medicines (WHO INN).
# K-OVERMASK-FIVE: the common words an abbreviation row inflects to. `FIV` is
# `FIV`, never `five`; `HIV` is `HIV`, never `hive`. `hives` stays masked: it
# is urticaria, a health word, and health fails closed.
# HEALTH-RECALL-1: common forms of a freelancer's mail or notes. Status words,
# treatments, scans, lab tests and the specialists whose name says the condition.
# HEALTH-EPONYM-1: conditions named after a person. A medical head joins the
# surname in code (`push_disease_names`); these are the fixed names it misses.
